definition: Streaks or wisps of precipitation — rain, snow, or ice crystals — that fall from a cloud but evaporate or sublimate before reaching the ground, visible as faint trailing curtains beneath the cloud base.
etymology: From Latin virga, meaning a rod, twig, or slender branch. Roman writers used it for any thin stripe or streak, and the word passed unchanged into meteorological Latin when observers needed a name for those ghostly rain-tails that dissolve in mid-air. The same root gave English verge and virgin via different routes.
usage: On a cold mid-November afternoon the clouds overhead were dramatic but delivered nothing: only virga, those pale grey brushstrokes dangling beneath them, spending themselves on dry air before a single drop could darken the pavement.
